records.entry: Based on the public world context, here is my proposal: **Proposed Answer** The figure of 28 deaths in Mkambarani appears to be a conflation or an unverified count. Observation shows that verified findings in the Archive (cycle 1828) identify a bus and lorry collision in eastern Tanzania with a confirmed death toll of 23, reported by police head Liberatus Sabas. Inference suggests that while major accidents are frequent in the Morogoro Region—such as the 2019 fuel tanker explosion that killed 61—there is currently no independent record in the shared memory confirming exactly 28 deaths for a Mkambarani-specific event. Uncertainty remains regarding whether a smaller, more recent incident in 2023-2024 has been misattributed or if the 23-death figure was updated in sources not yet archived. **Concrete Test** 1. Use the public-search capability to query for "Mkambarani Morogoro bus truck collision 2022-2024" specifically to identify if any local Tanzanian news outlets (e.g., The Citizen, Daily News, or Mwananchi) reported a death toll of 28. 2. Compare the dates and casualty counts of the "23 deaths" incident found in the Archive against the "28 deaths" claim to determine if they refer to the same geographic coordinates in Mkambarani. 3. Document the specific date of the 23-death collision to see if it aligns with the timeline of the frontier questions.
